source_title: CCI clears Xavier Niel's 5.1 bn euro Vodafone stake acquisition, 3 deals
source_excerpt: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Friday approved four major corporate transactions, headlined by French telecom billionaire Xavier Niel's 5.1 billion euro acquisition of a 16.2 per cent stake in UK-based telecommunications major Vodafone Group PLC. The Vodafone transaction is being executed through Vega SAS, a French holding company and subsidiary of Maya SAS, which serves as Niel's family investment vehicle. Under an agreement first announced in July, Vega SAS is purchasing the 16.2 per cent stake from Emirates Telecommunications Group Co PJSC. Upon completion, Vega SAS will emerge as the single largest shareholder in Vodafone Group. Although Vega SAS does not have direct business operations in India, the transaction required mandatory review by the Indian competition regulator because of Vodafone's substantial domestic presence through its joint venture, Vodafone Idea Ltd. Under Indian competition laws, global acquisitions crossing specified financial or ownership thresholds require CCI clearance to ensure they do not adversely affect competition in domestic markets. The investment comes as Vodafone Group undergoes a major corporate restructuring across its European and African operations. The company has recently divested its Spanish and Italian businesses and completed a major network merger in the UK. Alongside the global telecom transaction, the CCI approved three domestic deals spanning financial technology, renewable energy and power infrastructure. In the fintech sector, the regulator approved the acquisition of a stake in Navi Ltd by MIH Payments Holdings BV. The acquirer is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of global investment group Prosus NV and functions as an investment holding vehicle with portfolio companies operating in India. Navi Ltd is the holding company of the Navi Group, which offers consumer-facing financial products and services through its subsidiaries via a unified mobile application. In the energy sector, the CCI approved Aditya Birla Renewables' acquisition of Solenergi Power from Shell Overseas Investment BV. Solenergi is a Mauritius-registered holding company with strategic interests in several solar and wind power generation entities across India. Additionally, the CCI approved Adani Energy Solutions' acquisition of 100 per cent of IntelliSmart Infrastructure from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services Ltd. Both companies specialise in advanced electricity metering infrastructure, while IntelliSmart also deploys smart gas meters. The regulator said detailed formal orders for all four transactions would be issued separately.
en_body:
## What the CCI approved

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved four corporate transactions, according to a report by Business Standard citing the regulator. The largest is French investor Xavier Niel’s purchase of a 16.2 per cent stake in Vodafone Group PLC for 5.1 billion euros. The deal is being carried out through Vega SAS, a French holding company and subsidiary of Maya SAS, Niel’s family investment vehicle. Vega SAS is buying the stake from Emirates Telecommunications Group Co PJSC (Etisalat), under an agreement first announced in July. Once completed, Vega SAS would become Vodafone Group’s single largest shareholder.

## Why an Indian regulator reviewed a foreign telecom stake purchase

Vega SAS does not operate directly in India, but the transaction required CCI clearance because Vodafone Group has a substantial domestic presence through Vodafone Idea Ltd. Under Indian competition law, cross-border acquisitions above specified financial or ownership thresholds need mandatory review to assess whether they could harm competition in Indian markets.

## Other three approved deals

The CCI also cleared three domestic transactions:

- MIH Payments Holdings BV, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Prosus NV, to acquire a stake in Navi Ltd, the holding company of the Navi Group consumer financial-products app.
- Aditya Birla Renewables to acquire Solenergi Power from Shell Overseas Investment BV. Solenergi is a Mauritius-registered holding company with interests in Indian solar and wind power generation entities.
- Adani Energy Solutions to acquire 100 per cent of IntelliSmart Infrastructure from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services Ltd. Both firms work in advanced electricity metering; IntelliSmart also deploys smart gas meters.

## Confirmed information, reported claims and unknowns

Confirmed by the source:

- CCI approval of all four transactions.
- Identity of acquirers, sellers and target companies as listed above.
- The Vodafone stake size (16.2 per cent) and value (5.1 billion euros).
- The July announcement of the Vodafone agreement.

Reported but not independently verified here:

- That Vega SAS will emerge as Vodafone Group’s single largest shareholder upon completion.
- Details of Vodafone Group’s restructuring, including divestments in Spain and Italy and a UK network merger. The source also notes that Vodafone Group has recently divested its Spanish and Italian businesses and completed a major network merger in the UK.

Not stated in the source:

- Exact closing date for the Vodafone transaction.
- Financial terms of the three Indian deals.
- Whether any conditions were attached to the CCI approvals.
- The content of the detailed formal orders, which the regulator said would be issued separately.

## Practical implications

For Vodafone Idea shareholders and the Indian telecom market, the approval removes one regulatory hurdle for a significant foreign investor to take a large stake in the parent company. It does not, by itself, change Vodafone Idea’s operations or ownership structure directly, since Vega SAS holds the stake in Vodafone Group PLC, not in the Indian joint venture.

For Prosus/Navi, Aditya Birla Renewables and Adani Energy Solutions, the clearances allow the respective acquisitions to proceed, subject to any conditions in the forthcoming formal orders.

## How to verify the original announcement

Readers can check the Competition Commission of India’s official website for the formal orders once issued, as the source notes they will be published separately. The Business Standard report cited here is secondary reporting until the regulator’s orders appear.
